issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Farm: the problem statement explicitly requires initializing the internal ArrayList in a no-argument constructor, and the template/Main expects a no-arg Farm(), but the solution provides only a parameterized constructor Farm(int initialCapacity). This inconsistency can break student code/tests that instantiate Farm with the expected no-arg constructor and will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor for Farm that initializes the animals ArrayList (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Keep or optionally overload the existing parameterized constructor. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template/Main to require and use the same parameterized constructor; prefer adding the no-arg constructor to the solution to match the specification and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Farm constructor (students are instructed to initialize the ArrayList in a no-arg constructor and Main uses new Farm()), but the solution-only Farm implementation provides a single constructor Farm(int initialCapacity). This API mismatch (constructor signature difference) breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description/template usage and the provided solution, likely confusing students about which constructor to implement and how to instantiate Farm.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in the solution's Farm class that initializes the animals ArrayList (e.g., public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) so it matches the problem statement and the template Main usage; or, alternatively, update the problem statement and template examples to use Farm(int initialCapacity) consistently.
